## Example 3.13 {#fv4-example-3-13 .fv-lesson .relation-lesson }

```{=html}
<p>The line <span data-math="\ell"></span> passes through the points <span data-math="A(3,5,-4)"></span> and <span data-math="B(7,0,2)"></span>.</p><div class="relation-example-parts"><p>(i) Find a vector equation of the line <span data-math="\ell"></span>. <span class="relation-marks">[1 mark]</span></p><p>(ii) Determine, giving reasons, whether the point <span data-math="C(10,5,-2)"></span> lies on the line <span data-math="\ell"></span>. <span class="relation-marks">[2 marks]</span></p></div>
```

<div class="booklet-cue">Booklet Example 3.13 · p. 57 · 2024 HSC Mathematics Extension 2 Q12(e)</div>

::: {.notes}
(i) AB=(4,−5,6), so $\underset{\sim}{r}=(3,5,-4)+\lambda(4,-5,6)$, λ real. (ii) For C, x gives λ=7/4, y gives λ=0, and z gives λ=1/3. There is no common parameter, so C does not lie on the line. Equivalently AC=(7,0,2) is not a scalar multiple of AB. A clear contradiction from any two components suffices; do not imply every inconsistent value must be computed once failure is established. The marks are copied from the supplied booklet. Use this as consolidation.
:::
